title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, and RevRec Guidance (2024 Q4)
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary

This guidance consolidates Redwood Inference's core policies and operational procedures for budgeting and forecasting, procurement and approvals, contracts lifecycle, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business owners responsible for planning, committing spend, executing agreements, and recognizing revenue.

Scope

Applies to: all internal teams that request or manage budget, submit purchase requests, enter into contracts, or own product/pricing changes that affect revenue recognition or billing. This doc covers: annual and quarterly budgeting, rolling forecasting, procurement approval thresholds, standard contract review steps, and RevRec rules for subscription and usage-based billing.

Key definitions

- Budget: approved allocation for a fiscal period (annual or quarterly) for a functional area or project.
- Forecast: rolling 12-month projection updated monthly or quarterly depending on team.
- Capex vs Opex: Capex refers to capital expenditures (capitalizable hardware/software licenses); Opex covers recurring operating expenses.
- RevRec: revenue recognition; how and when Redwood records revenue for contracts and services provided.
- PO: purchase order issued by Finance to vendors for approved procurement.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting process

Overview:
- Annual budget cycle runs from October (planning) to December (board approval) for the following fiscal year.
- Quarterly reforecast is required within 3 weeks after quarter close or on significant variance triggers (>5% ARR movement).

Roles & ownership:
- Finance: consolidation, guidance, scenario modeling, and board deliverables.
- Product and Sales: revenue forecasts, pricing changes, contract levers.
- Engineering and Infra: capacity/cost forecasts (GPU-hours, cloud egress, licensing).
- Managers: submit and defend team budgets and monthly forecast updates.

Steps (standard):
1. Planning kickoff (Oct 1–Oct 15): Finance publishes templates and assumptions.
2. Department submissions (Oct 15–Nov 7): SLT and teams submit budgets with supporting narratives and KPIs.
3. Iteration and consolidation (Nov 8–Nov 30): Finance runs scenarios, adjusts for corporate goals.
4. Final review and board packet (Dec 1–Dec 15): CFO and CEO review; board materials prepared.
5. Quarterly reforecast (quarter+3 weeks): teams submit updates; Finance consolidates and publishes variance commentary.

Forecasting best practices:
- Maintain rolling 12-month forecast with drivers: new customer bookings, churn, average revenue per user, and usage profile for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments.
- Include sensitivity analysis for major levers: model hosting price changes, GPU spot availability, and major customer contract renewals.
- Document assumptions explicitly in the template (growth rate, renewal probabilities, pricing changes) and retain prior assumptions for audit.

2) Procurement and purchase approvals

Approval thresholds (effective immediately):
- Team lead approval required for requests < $5k Opex.
- Director+ approval required for $5k–$50k Opex or any single-year contract > $25k.
- VP Finance or CFO approval required for > $50k Opex, multi-year commitments > $100k, or any Capex > $25k.
- Legal review required for any contract with non-standard terms, data residency implications, indemnity/limitation clauses, or vendor access to customer data.

Procurement steps (ordered):
1. Intake: submit request in procurement system with business justification, cost center, GL account, and preferred vendor.
2. Sourcing: Procurement evaluates vendor options for purchases > $25k (competitive quotes required).
3. Approvals: Obtain approvals per thresholds above.
4. PO issuance: Finance issues PO only after approvals and attached contract (if applicable).
5. Receipt & invoice: Ops or requestor confirms receipt; Finance matches invoice to PO for payment.

Required attachments for vendor/contract requests:
- Statement of work or product spec (if applicable).
- Estimated TCO (total cost of ownership) for multi-year commitments (include hardware maintenance, power, network, headcount support).
- Security & compliance assessment (for vendors with data access): brief from Security & Compliance team or link to vendor questionnaire.

Procurement table (text representation):
- Small purchases: < $5k — internal card or petty purchase, one approver.
- Mid purchases: $5k–$25k — director approval, one quote recommended.
- Large purchases: $25k–$100k — VP/Finance approval, 2–3 competitive quotes, procurement involvement.
- Strategic purchases: > $100k — executive review, legal & security assessments mandatory.

3) Contracts & legal process

Standard lifecycle:
1. Request & intake: Requestor opens contract request in CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management) system and selects template (SaaS, Professional Services, Vendor).
2. Initial review (Legal): Legal triages template selection and highlights non-standard terms.
3. Commercial review (Finance/Product): Review pricing, billing terms, order form, revenue recognition implications.
4. Negotiation & redlines: Legal manages counterparty negotiations and maintains version control in CLM.
5. Approval & signature: Countersigned copies stored in CLM; Finance triggers PO (if vendor) or billing setup (if customer).
6. Post-signature obligations: Assign owner to monitor deliverables, milestones, and renewal windows.

Key contractual checkpoints:
- Data handling and residency: any clause allowing vendor access to customer or company data must be reviewed by Security & Compliance.
- Indemnities & liability caps: Legal and Finance must sign off on deviations from standard caps.
- Termination & refund: Ensure refund/termination language aligns with billing system capabilities for proration.
- Change-of-control/assignment: Escalate to executive sponsor when present.

Contract playbook (quick checklist):
- Use approved Redwood template where possible.
- No non-standard indemnity or unlimited liability.
- Ensure SLA and uptime obligations have measurable metrics and remediation terms.
- Identify revenue recognition triggers in Commercial Schedule for Sales/Finance to implement in RevRec.

4) Revenue recognition & billing policies

Principles:
- Revenue is recognized when performance obligations are satisfied and collectibility is probable, consistent with ASC 606 (or applicable local GAAP).
- Separate distinct performance obligations in contracts (e.g., hosted API access, dedicated capacity reservations, and professional services) and recognize revenue for each when delivered.

Common scenarios and treatment:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize as services are delivered. Usage is measured daily; revenue is recognized monthly based on recorded usage and invoiced in the following billing cycle.
- Dedicated capacity (reservations/committed capacity): Fixed recurring revenue is recognized ratably over the term of the commitment. If there are upfront implementation services that are distinct, recognize separately when delivered.
- Private deployments (license + services): Evaluate whether software license is distinct (potentially upfront recognition if perpetual license and delivery complete) versus hosted service (ratable). Consult Finance for capitalization criteria.
- Professional services (implementation/customization): Recognize over time as services rendered (percentage-of-completion or milestones) if measurable, otherwise on delivery.

Invoicing and billing cadence:
- Standard customers: monthly invoicing in arrears for usage; net-30 payment terms unless otherwise negotiated.
- Enterprise contracts: may include upfront prepayments, multi-year invoicing, or milestone-based billing. Finance must map payment schedules to RevRec allocation.

Credit & collections:
- New enterprise customers require credit check and reference checks for > $250k ARR exposure.
- Collections escalate to Legal for invoices > 60 days past due; Sales and Customer Success must be looped for account context.

RevRec operational controls:
- All signed contracts and order forms must be uploaded to CLM and linked to the billing system before revenue is recorded.
- Monthly RevRec close checklist: reconcile contract schedule, billing system invoices, and deferred revenue ledger.
- Deviations from standard recognition (e.g., custom milestones, variable consideration with significant estimates) must be documented and approved by the Controller.

Examples (short):
- Example A: Customer purchases a $120k annual dedicated capacity plan billed annually upfront. Revenue: recognize $10k monthly over 12 months if there are no remaining performance obligations. Deferred revenue = $120k on receipt, released monthly.
- Example B: Usage invoice $15k generated for March usage, billed April 10, collected April 22: Recognize $15k in March (service period), invoice in April; record accounts receivable on invoice date, match to revenue period in RevRec.

5) Controls, audit, and reporting

- Documentation: retain procurement rationale, quotes, approvals, and contracts for 7 years (or longer if required by contract).
- Internal controls: segregation of duties between requestor, approver, and Finance for PO issuance.
- Audit readiness: maintain a versioned trail of forecasts, templates, and assumptions in the finance drive and link to Confluence pages.

6) Exception handling and escalations

Common exceptions:
- Emergency procurement (e.g., critical open-source dependency fix requiring immediate vendor engagement): Seek VP Finance and Head of Security verbal approval, then follow up with formal approvals within 48 hours.
- Non-standard contract clause requested by customer (e.g., custom indemnity): Legal to route to General Counsel; executive sponsor to approve deviations above $500k ARR impact.

Appendices

A. Budget template fields (to be used in planning workbook):
- Cost center, owner, FY24 request, FY25 request, headcount FTEs, GPU hours estimate, cloud egress TB, 3-year TCO, business justification, KPIs impacted.

B. Standard contract templates and locations:
- SaaS Master Services Agreement (MSA) — CLM: /templates/msa-saas
- Vendor Purchase Agreement — CLM: /templates/vendor-po
- Professional Services SOW — CLM: /templates/sow

C. RevRec checklist for Finance close:
- Contracts uploaded to CLM and linked to billing system.
- Deferred revenue = opening + billings - recognized.
- Variable consideration assessed and documented.
- Controller sign-off for any manual adjustments.

Revision history
- 2024-10-15: Document created (planning cycle guidance).
- 2024-12-18: Updated procurement thresholds and procurement table.
- 2025-01-20: Clarified RevRec treatments for private deployments and added example scenarios.

Questions or support

For clarifications or to request exceptions, contact Finance (finance-ops@redwood.ai) or Legal (legal-ops@redwood.ai).

End of document.
